transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Lena Morris (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Veridian Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Security), Evan Park (Product)
Shared: Deck (Console walkthrough): http://bit.ly/redwood-console-demo, Security pack: /redwood/security-pack.pdf (shared after)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown with discussion about Dedicated vs Hosted and private VPC/KMS requirements. Agreed to run POC benchmark in Veridian infra; Redwood to send pricing and security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: all right hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, uh with diego our se, we'll walk through the console side — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown. do i have permission to record?
[00:12] Priya: yep that's fine, thanks lena.
[00:15] Diego: great, i'll share screen, um pardon any small typo in the consle name in the deck — uhh quick note on agenda.
[00:30] Diego: okay so starting on the Console overview, the top left is token-level usage, token cost, and per-route breakdowns; we try to make cost attribution as close to the route as possible so product teams can own their spend.
[01:02] Marcus: quick question, how do you map which tokens belong to which internal routes? we have a mix of server-side and client-side calls.
[01:18] Diego: good q — we support route tags (route_id, env, team) and you can attach them via the API header or SDK. the console then aggregates by route tag, model, and time window. if you don't tag, we fall back to endpoint name; there's also a token attribution export.
[01:45] Priya: is there support for span-level tracing to tie api calls back to our traces (open-telemetry)?
[01:55] Diego: yes, we have trace hooks and you can ingest trace ids into the request metadata. we show a link in the per-route view to open the trace in your tracing system — small caveat: the trace link is a pointer, not a full trace ingest.
[02:20] Lena: jumping into the usage analytics chart — here you can see 7-day rolling tokens, cost by model family, and latency percentiles. we also surface an efficiency metric — tokens per useful token, roughly speaking, to catch prompt inflation.
[02:49] Sofia: security question, are these dashboards multi-tenant? like can we limit which teams see which routes?
[03:00] Diego: yes RBAC at route level, SSO/SAML integration, and audit logs. audit logs show who changed rollout config, model pinning, and who viewed cost reports.
[03:18] Sofia: and encryption at rest? KMS/HSM?
[03:24] Lena: we support customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated via KMS. for hosted we offer envelope encryption with our keys, but customer-managed keys are available for Dedicated and Private — note: you'll want to confirm in the security pack for exact legal language.
[03:45] Priya: can you show per-route cost breakdown, like if we have a 'summarize-claim' route vs 'patient-qna' route?
[03:56] Diego: yep switching to per-route dashboards — here, route list on the left, click a route, view token breakdown, model used, average per-request cost, and the cost components (compute, model license if applicable, and infra overhead).
[04:22] Diego: the console also surfaces suggested optimizations from Redwood Optimize — e.g. switch to a quantized model variant, enable prefix caching, or change batching policy to reduce per-token cost while preserving 95th p99 latency SLOs.
[04:50] Marcus: how granular are suggestions? will it say 'use model-x q4 8-bit' or more generic?
[05:01] Diego: it's model-specific; we'll recommend model variants we host (e.g., llama-2-q8, mix-quant) and also config suggestions (batch size, max tokens, KV cache TTL).
[05:22] Priya: we're sensitive to hallucinations — do recommendations include quality regressions checks?
[05:32] Lena: yes, Optimize ties suggestions to quality evals — you can attach a prompt set and it runs regression checks, flags potential quality drop, and shows a tradeoff curve cost vs quality.
[05:58] Evan: for our timeline, we're looking at a pilot in prod infra in july — what's typical POC size?
[06:07] Diego: typical pilot is 1-2 routes, 2-4 weeks, run benchmarks against representative traffic. we can run both hosted and dedicated comparisons; for private we mirror your infra.
[06:28] Priya: Perf — can you run microbenchmarks? we have variable sequence lengths; KV-cache behavior matters.
[06:40] Diego: yes, Diego: we can reproduce sequence length distribution, and the benchmark plan includes cold and warm KV-cache runs, batching profiles. we'll share a benchmark template.
[06:55] Lena: security again — SOC2, iso?
[06:58] Sofia: yes please.
[07:04] Lena: we are SOC2 Type II and pursuing ISO certifications; security pack will include SOC2 report, penetration test summary, data flow diagrams, and KMS/HSM integration notes.
[07:22] Marcus: curious on cost model — for hosted api, is it purely per-token? do you show infra cost split?
[07:33] Diego: hosted is per-token plus optional features. the console shows a token-level cost breakdown and an estimated infra overhead; for Dedicated there's a reserved capacity cost line item and utilization metrics. we also show amortized GPU cost per token in the cost explorer.
[08:02] Priya: what about routing/fallbacks — if primary model is down or capacity constrained, does console show failover uses and costs?
[08:13] Diego: yes, routing policies and fallbacks are logged. the console has a route timeline showing model switches, fallback counts, and associated cost delta.
[08:30] Evan: do you allow per-route throttles to enforce cost budgets?
[08:36] Diego: yes, you can set per-route budgets and soft/hard limits; soft limits generate alerts and suggest autoscale configuration.
[08:50] Priya: for compliance we need audit trails for actual prompts — retention and redaction options?
[08:58] Lena: you can configure logs to redact PII at ingestion or store full transcripts under Private deployments; retention configurable per-org with retention policies in Console.
[09:18] Marcus: can you demo a cost anomaly alert? we had a 3x spike due to a runaway loop last month and need to detect it quickly.
[09:27] Diego: sure — switching to Alerts page — we have anomaly detection on tokens/sec, cost/day, and per-route qps; thresholds can be static or use adaptive baselines. here's an example alert we send to Slack and PagerDuty with a direct link to the offending route and sample requests.
[09:55] Priya: sample requests meaning — do you store request/response payloads?
[10:03] Diego: depends on retention config; sample requests are snippets with identifiers, not full payloads unless you enable request capture. you can also forward them to your S3 for analysis.
[10:18] Lena: now walking through the cost explorer — you can break down cost by model, by route, by tag, or by team. the UI supports exporting CSV and a cost allocation API to push to your internal billing system.
[10:40] Marcus: can we map costs to our internal department codes? we use a custom chargeback system.
[10:46] Diego: yes, you can send route tags that match your department codes and pull via cost allocation API; we also support direct BigQuery export for customers using GCP.
[11:05] Priya: how do you attribute tokens for streaming responses, is there partial token accounting?
[11:12] Diego: streaming tokens are accounted as they are emitted; we show breakdowns by partial responses and aggregate to request-level cost. minor jitter in timestamps may show up but cost is consistent.
[11:35] Evan: people sometimes misuse a heavy model for trivial tasks (eg summary using 70B). can console recommend smaller models automatically?
[11:44] Diego: yep, Optimize can propose a model swap with expected cost savings and estimated quality impact; it can also create a canary rollout to evaluate in prod on a small percentage of traffic.
[12:05] Priya: about canaries — do you support weighted traffic splits and automatic rollback?
[12:12] Diego: yes, canary rollouts with metrics monitoring (latency, p99, error, quality evals). you can set auto-rollback if key metrics cross thresholds.
[12:30] Marcus: for Dedicated, what's the typical autoscale policy? can it burst to hosted if capacity hit?
[12:38] Lena: Dedicated supports configured autoscale with burst capacity options that can spill to hosted if you opt in; there's a policy to limit spill and you get cost breakout for any spilled requests.
[12:55] Priya: any caveats on data residency? we have EU patient data that must not leave region.
[13:03] Diego: Private deployments inside your VPC or on-prem can ensure data never leaves region; for Hosted we have regional endpoints but if you need absolute guarantee, Private or Dedicated w/ VPC is recommended.
[13:22] Evan: okay big question on cost modeling for POC — can you provide an expected cost per 10k requests for our 'patient-summary' route with average 800 tokens in prompt and 400 tokens response?
[13:36] Diego: we can estimate — we'll need model choice, quantization, and whether KV cache is warm. rough ballpark we can send in the pricing sheet; for accuracy we'll run a benchmark with your payload.
[13:55] Lena: moving on — demoing per-route dashboard drilldown: clicking patient-summary route shows timeline, cost per hour, top consumers (service accounts and IPs), and quality regressions flagged by eval sets.
[14:20] Priya: nice, can we tag requests with user_id for debugging?
[14:25] Diego: yes include user_id in metadata, we don't index PII by default unless you opt-in; it shows up in the sample request with redaction options.
[14:40] Marcus: what about model license fees, are those surfaced?
[14:45] Diego: if using a licensed model through Redwood catalog, license fees are shown as a separate cost component. for open models it's compute-only.
[15:02] Priya: is there an api to pull per-route cost so we can consume it in our finance system?
[15:08] Diego: yes cost allocation API and CSV export; you can programmatically request a cost snapshot per date range.
[15:28] Evan: are there per-token cost tiers? like discounts after X tokens?
[15:33] Lena: usage tiers and committed reserved capacity for Dedicated are supported; the pricing sheet will show tiered discounts and commit levels.
[15:50] Priya: how quickly does console reflect changes after we redeploy a new model?
[15:57] Diego: metrics are near realtime — most dashboards update within 30-60s; some aggregated views are on a 5-min rollup.
[16:15] Marcus: on metrics retention — how long do you keep detailed token-level logs?
[16:21] Lena: default retention is 90 days for detailed logs; longer retention is an add-on. for Private deployments you control retention.
[16:40] Priya: ok let's talk about the POC benchmarks — what exact artifacts do you need from us?
[16:47] Diego: sample prompts, traffic histogram (qps, seq len distro), SLI targets (p95/p99 latency SLO), and security requirements. we'll produce a benchmark plan and expected cost sheet.
[17:05] Priya: i'll collate that.
[17:08] Evan: can you show the UI for Optimize suggestions again?
[17:12] Diego: sure — Optimize feed shows active suggestions, expected savings, quality delta, and a 'apply as canary' button which sets up the rollout automatically.
[17:34] Lena: one small note — some proper nouns might be mis-transcribed in the recording, apologies in advance.
[17:40] Priya: no worries.
[18:00] Diego: switching to a cost anomaly example — here's a spike caused by a bot loop, the system auto-detected and opened a ticket, we traced to a particular service account. links to the raw requests are here (sanitized).
[18:25] Marcus: do you keep a map of which model-kernel combos are used per-request? we tune kernel selection for latency.
[18:33] Diego: yes runtime picks kernels per model and sequence length; we log the kernel variant and make it visible for performance debugging. small risk: kernel names can look cryptic in the logs.
[18:55] Priya: how do you handle streaming real-time? we need sub-second for some use-cases.
[19:01] Diego: streaming latencies depend on network and model; our runtime supports incremental output and low-latency routes; you can set a low-latency profile to prioritize small batches.
[19:20] Evan: if we want to try Dedicated, how long to provision?
[19:25] Lena: Dedicated provisioning lead time depends on region and capacity, typically 2-6 weeks; on-prem Private timelines vary. for urgent pilots we can use hosted or a shared dedicated pool for initial testing.
[19:45] Priya: one more security question — do you support VPC peering or private link?
[19:51] Diego: we support VPC peering, PrivateLink (cloud provider specific), and on-prem connectors for private deployments.
[20:10] Marcus: rollback story — if a model rollout increases hallucinations, can we automatically fallback to the previous model?
[20:18] Diego: yes auto-rollback based on quality evals and error/latency thresholds; you can also configure a hard rollback if any customer-visible errors occur.
[20:40] Priya: about the eval sets — can they be encrypted at rest with our KMS?
[20:46] Lena: yes for Private and Dedicated eval artifacts can use customer-managed KMS; hosted offers envelope encryption but not CMK.
[21:05] Evan: ok this is all very helpful. can we get a sample export of per-route costs?
[21:11] Diego: i'll export a CSV sample and share it after the call.
[21:20] Priya: and the benchmark template?
[21:23] Diego: yes will include benchmark template and load scripts.
[21:30] Lena: recap — redwood to send pricing + SKUs, security pack (SOC2, KMS notes), demo recording, sample cost export, and benchmark plan. Veridian to share sample prompts, traffic profiles, and compliance questions. we'll schedule the POC for week of 6/29.
[21:55] Sofia: one last compliance tidbit — we need to confirm data residency for EU patients; will follow up in the security doc.
[22:05] Lena: noted.
[22:18] Marcus: thanks everyone.
[22:22] Priya: thanks!
[22:25] Diego: thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcription has natural speech artifacts and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "consle"). Links/files to be attached to the CRM activity: demo recording, pricing sheet, security pack, benchmark plan, example cost CSV.

End of transcript.
